newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended higher on Monday, erasing earlier losses sparked by a Socialist win at French elections on Sunday. But dealers were surprised by the market's strength.
"To me there's no apparent reason for the market to be so strong," said Emilio Sainz, a dealer at Natwest in Madrid.
"But I guess it will go higher tomorrow," he said adding that he expected yields at the Treasury auctions would fall more than expected.
Spain's Treasury is auctioning three- and ten-year bonds on Tuesday. It will sell five- and 15-year bonds, and six-month bills on Wednesday.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended at around 74 basis points, well off the 81 bps of this morning, but little changed from Friday's end at 75 basis points.
Other dealers in Madrid said that after the over-reaction to the French vote, the market was now looking for news from Germany on Bonn's decision to approve a gold revaluation plan.

Chartists said a closing level above key resistance at 115 was supporting the view that long term bond futures could start Tuesday climbing higher. They peg next resistance at 115.75. -- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
